subject: Draft public copy: DPA & cross-border data flow explainer
messages:
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Draft public copy: DPA & cross-border data flow explainer

Team —

I'm attaching a short set of public-facing snippets we want to surface in the Console (help tooltip + DPA landing) and the API docs about cross-border transfers, subprocessors, and retention. Goal: make it simple for EU customers to understand safeguards (SCCs, SCC+whatever), what subprocessors we use, and what data may be retained for operational reasons (cache/logs).

Attached: "console_tooltip_snippets.txt" (3 options per snippet) and a PDF with DPA v3 redlines for legal. Quick asks:
- Kimberly: can you review the two short snippets (A/B) and confirm legal language we can publish without opening a big procurement conversation?
- Marcus: can you prepare Console tooltip copy and limit to 2 lines (max 160 chars) and mark where we should link to full DPA?
- Naomi: flag any telemetry/observability mentions that need customer opt-in.

Draft snippets (very rough):
1) API docs short: "Redwood may transfer personal data outside the EEA to support hosted inference. Transfers are protected by EU-approved safeguards; see our DPA for details."
2) Console tooltip short: "Data sent to hosted API may be processed outside your region under standard safeguards (SCCs). See DPA & subprocessors list."
3) Retention note: "We retain request metadata and temporary KV cache for up to 30 days to support reliability and billing; prompt content is not stored long-term unless you enable request logging."

Please add inline redlines into the PDF or reply with firmed language. If we can get legal sign-off this week I will share with Acme (they asked for clearer copy).

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Content Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_v3_redlines.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), console_tooltip_snippets.txt (plain text)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft public copy: DPA & cross-border data flow explainer

Thanks, Soojin — good concise start. A few legal suggestions and constraints to keep us safe on public language:

1) Avoid the phrase "may transfer" in isolation — it reads as permissive. Prefer: "We may transfer personal data outside the EEA where necessary to provide the Service, and will do so only with appropriate safeguards (for example, Standard Contractual Clauses)."

2) Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) are still the clearest, but we should not promise specific legal mechanisms in case of future regime changes. Proposed line: "Transfers are protected by EU-approved safeguards (e.g., SCCs) or other lawful mechanisms as applicable."

3) Subprocessors: we can and should say we publish a current subprocessors list and that subprocessors have access only to data necessary to provide the service. Do not say "only metadata" unless verified per vendor.

4) Retention: "temporary KV cache for up to 30 days" is OK but we must define "KV cache" in the DPA. Suggest: "short-lived operational caches (generally under 30 days) to support performance and correctness."

5) DPA redlines: I've inserted comments in dpa_v3_redlines.pdf. Two redline items need product confirmation: (a) whether we can commit to a 30-day max for all cache types, and (b) whether logs ever contain unredacted prompt content for Hosted customers.

Next step: I can sign off on high-level public copy once product confirms the above and Marcus produces the tooltip with an explicit link to the DPA. I will provide a one-paragraph legal-approved snippet for the Console landing page.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Draft public copy: DPA & cross-border data flow explainer

Appreciate the quick review, Kimberly — clear guidance. Marcus, can you take the legal-approved one-paragraph and produce: (A) Console tooltip (2 lines, 160 chars), (B) Console DPA landing intro (1 short paragraph), and (C) API docs sentence variant (50-90 chars) we can include in the header?

Notes for Marcus:
- Link target for "DPA" should be: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-redlines (will move to /legal when live)
- On subprocessors we should include a short link: "Full subprocessors list" (public URL) rather than enumerating in the tooltip.
- Naomi: can you confirm whether any internal logs (SRE/observability) contain raw prompt text for hosted customers when request-logging is not explicitly enabled? If they do, we need to say so and propose mitigation.

I will also reach out to Acme legal with a concise draft they can review (see below). If Kimberly can paste the one-paragraph legal-approved copy into a reply that would be great.

Proposed outreach to Acme (draft to send):

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: dana.miller@acme-payments.com, acme-legal@acme-payments.com
Subject: Proposed public copy for DPA & transfers

Dana — thanks for flagging clarity needs. Attached are two short versions of public copy and our DPA with redlines. High-level: we use EU-approved safeguards (e.g., SCCs) for transfers, publish subprocessors, and retain short-lived operational caches (generally under 30 days). Can you confirm whether that level of detail will meet Acme's procurement/legal needs; happy to jump on a short call this week.

Thanks — Soojin

Hi Soojin — thanks for sending this through and for the quick turnaround. A few points from Acme's side:

1) Can you confirm exactly which subprocessors are currently used for Hosted API (we need vendor names and country locations)? A link to the live list is fine.
2) Logs: please clarify whether logs or observability traces might contain customer prompts by default. If they do, we need confirmation of retention windows and access controls.
3) Retention: 30 days for "operational caches" is acceptable in principle; we need to see the DPA redline for confirmation.

If you can provide the redlined DPA and the live subprocessors link, we will take that to procurement. If needed, we can set a 30-minute sync tomorrow to close this quickly.

Forwarding previous message below for context.

Best,
Dana Miller
Head of Security & Privacy, Acme Payments
